stories.title: Accenture plans voluntary departures in Portugal
stories.summary: Accenture is preparing a voluntary departure programme for its Lisbon teams, aiming to reduce its workforce by approximately 950 employees by early 2027. The affected staff currently provide Trust and Safety services for Meta. Around 1,400 employees are eligible to participate in the process.

stories.title: BofA resumes coverage of Accenture with Buy rating
stories.summary: BofA Securities resumed coverage of Accenture on November 19 with a Buy rating and a 288 dollar price target. The analyst cited enterprise AI demand and industry consolidation as factors supporting the company's growth case. The stock gained a fresh analyst catalyst during the week.

stories.title: Accenture wins 61 million dollar Department of Energy contract
stories.summary: Accenture Federal Services was awarded a 69-month task to provide application operations and maintenance support to the Department of Energy. The contract is valued at approximately 61 million dollars. The firm aims to power reinvention across the federal government using proven commercial solutions and new technologies.

Qantas to cut 850 jobs in Accenture outsourcing deal
stories.summary: Qantas will cut 850 jobs under an outsourcing deal with Accenture, according to the Australian Greens. The party stated that hundreds of roles will move offshore as part of an AI overhaul. Qantas recorded a 1.29 billion dollar profit in the last financial year.

stories.title: Accenture secures 10 million dollar IRS database contract
stories.summary: Accenture Federal Services was awarded a two-year task to provide database support for the Internal Revenue Service. The contract is valued at approximately 9.7 million dollars. The firm continues to provide mission expertise and new technologies to federal agencies under its 2027 Elev8 GovCon designation.

Report projects 1.2 trillion dollar machinery market for India
stories.summary: India targets a 1.2 trillion dollar capital goods industry by 2047, according to a report by the Confederation of Indian Industry and Boston Consulting Group. The projection relies on domestic manufacturing growth in AI, semiconductors, and defence. The country aims to cut imports to boost local production.

stories.title: Accenture report identifies global consumer trends
stories.summary: Accenture's 20th annual Life Trends report identifies five macro trends regarding consumer expectations in the age of AI. The findings indicate that while people embrace technological progress, they are increasingly concerned about retaining control over their choices. Consumers are using AI for search, content creation, and earning.

stories.title: Bain examines agentic commerce in retail
stories.summary: Retailers are evaluating how AI reshapes shopping behavior as the year concludes. Bain and Company reports that shoppers now start with AI, which selects the best fit rather than the biggest retailer. This shift provides an edge to companies that adapt to AI-driven search and answer models.

stories.title: Accenture survey finds AI-generated ads unpopular in India
stories.summary: Fifty-six percent of respondents in India said brands using AI for advertising appear lazy, careless, and cheap, according to an Accenture Song report. Fifty-five percent of those surveyed also found their social media feeds becoming irrelevant. Consumers are reportedly seeking more distinctive voices and direct ties with creators.

stories.title: Accenture report on AI and consumer control
stories.summary: Accenture's annual Life Trends report finds that consumers are embracing AI for search and creation but resisting the loss of control associated with digital experiences. The report suggests that while people want technology to help them live longer, they are exhausted by the synthetic sameness of current digital tools.

stories.title: McKinsey report links sustainability to cash flow
stories.summary: Sustainability risks and opportunities could impact companies' long-term free cash flow by up to 20 percent of their EBITDA, according to a new McKinsey report. The firm suggests sustainability has become a key business priority, requiring chief executive officers to take direct responsibility for their strategies.

stories.title: Pharma GCCs contribute 10.5 billion dollars to India economy
stories.summary: Global Capacity Centres established by pharmaceutical companies in India contribute up to 10.5 billion dollars in gross value added, according to an OPPI and EY report. The centers are estimated to employ 120,000 professionals. The broader GCC sector created 10.4 million jobs in 2025.

stories.title: Global luxury market holds at 1.5 trillion euros
stories.summary: Global luxury spending is expected to reach 1.5 trillion euros in 2026, remaining flat or growing up to 2 percent compared to 2025. Bain and Company reports the market has expanded by 16 to 22 percent since 2019, despite geopolitical tensions and macroeconomic uncertainty.

stories.title: Bain survey finds high demand for healthcare convenience
stories.summary: Eighty-four percent of consumers expect greater healthcare convenience, according to a Bain and Company survey. The report notes that one in five doctors is considering leaving their employer due to burnout and workload. Asia-Pacific healthcare systems are increasingly looking toward AI-enabled support to manage these pressures.

stories.title: Oliver Wyman to acquire Synpulse
stories.summary: Oliver Wyman has agreed to acquire Synpulse, a technology consulting and AI platform company. The firms have previously worked together on client projects. The transaction is expected to close in early 2027, subject to regulatory approvals. Financial terms were not disclosed. The firms are currently familiar with each other.

stories.title: Valterra Platinum signs BPO deal with Deloitte
stories.summary: Valterra Platinum has signed a business process outsourcing agreement with Deloitte. The deal involves the transfer of more than 130 employees to the Big Four firm, which will take over several corporate support functions. Valterra Platinum became an independent company in 2025 following its separation from Anglo American.

stories.title: Teneo hires Mike Granowski as senior managing director
stories.summary: Teneo has hired Mike Granowski as a senior managing director in its energy and infrastructure practice. Based in Chicago, Granowski joins from Roland Berger. He brings over 25 years of experience in energy and utilities, including work with utility companies, OEMs, and investors on strategy and capital programs.

stories.title: Mace Consult appoints Mario Sawaya as president for Americas
stories.summary: Mace Consult has appointed Mario Sawaya as president for the Americas. Based in Seattle, Sawaya will oversee the firm's regional business, including capital programs like the Hudson Tunnel Project. He brings over 20 years of experience in the architecture, engineering, and construction sector to the role.

Oliver Wyman to buy Synpulse in AI consulting push
stories.summary: Oliver Wyman has agreed to acquire Synpulse, a technology consulting and AI platform company. The deal is expected to close in early 2027, pending regulatory approvals. The firms already work together on client transformations. Oliver Wyman notes that clients now want partners who can help at every stage.

stories.title: Oliver Wyman to acquire Synpulse
stories.summary: Oliver Wyman has entered an agreement to acquire Synpulse, a global technology and AI company specializing in financial services. The transaction is expected to close in early 2027, subject to customary conditions. Financial terms were not disclosed. The acquisition aims to expand Oliver Wyman's AI engineering and implementation capabilities.

stories.title: Brian Elliott joins QuantumBlack AI leadership
stories.summary: McKinsey veteran Brian Elliott has joined QuantumBlack to co-lead EcliptOS, the firm's newly launched AI operating system. EcliptOS is described as a modular system designed to integrate AI across organizations. Elliott brings over 20 years of experience from McKinsey, where he previously held various global leadership roles.

stories.title: PwC India says job market demands specialized skills
stories.summary: PwC India chairperson Sanjeev Krishan said companies are increasingly seeking professionals with specialized skills to deliver measurable business outcomes. He noted a shift toward outcome-based pricing, where clients pay for results rather than hours worked. PwC hires between 3,500 and 4,000 people in India annually.

stories.title: EngenX highlights industrial AI for smart factories
stories.summary: EngenX is promoting industrial AI, including digital twins and predictive maintenance, to improve manufacturing productivity. The company aims to support India's goal of raising manufacturing's contribution to GDP to 25 percent by 2035. Its platform focuses on machine data and operational intelligence for factory transformation.

stories.title: EY India unveils AI agents for enterprise operations
stories.summary: EY India has launched a suite of AI agents for finance, cybersecurity, and supply chain management. The company claims these agents move beyond automating single tasks to support full, interconnected processes. The tools are designed to improve data quality and strengthen cyber incident response for enterprise clients.

stories.title: India consumer durables market projected to grow
stories.summary: A report by BCG and the CII projects India's consumer durables market will reach 3 lakh to 3.25 lakh crore by 2030. Growth is attributed to rising household incomes and financing access. The report notes that a significant share of this opportunity could still be met through imports.

stories.title: Education remains top cause for Indian philanthropists
stories.summary: Education attracted 4,188 crore in donations in 2026, remaining the most supported cause among India's leading philanthropists. According to the EdelGive Hurun India Philanthropy List, education accounted for 36 percent of total donations. Some 200 individuals supported the sector, with 95 identifying it as their primary cause.

stories.title: Manufacturing sector marks 80 years of independence
stories.summary: India's manufacturing sector has expanded through reforms including the Production Linked Incentive scheme and the National Logistics Policy. The government aims to position the nation as a global hub for industries ranging from defence to electronics. The sector is now focused on maintaining momentum for self-reliance.

Schneider Electric and BCG partner on AI manufacturing
stories.summary: Schneider Electric and BCG have formed a collaboration to accelerate AI-enabled smart manufacturing in India. The organizations will combine infrastructure with digital transformation expertise to help manufacturers scale Industry 4.0 solutions. The partnership aims to support India's goal of becoming a developed economy by 2047.

stories.title: Retail sales growth varies by region in India
stories.summary: KPMG's Festive Retail Pulse 2026 report shows retail sales grew 10 percent in the west and 9 percent in the south. The report notes a shift in consumer spending toward apparel and footwear. September growth was attributed to pre-festive momentum rather than the full impact of the season.

stories.title: SP Jain Institute of Management and Research wins EY-Parthenon competition
stories.summary: SP Jain Institute of Management and Research, Mumbai won the Quest EY-Parthenon Business Case Competition 2026. The event tasked students with developing strategic solutions for an AI-driven world. EY-Parthenon India reports that Gen Z talent now accounts for more than 50 percent of its local workforce.

stories.title: PwC India says experienced professionals are in higher demand
stories.summary: PwC India Chairperson Sanjeev Krishan says jobs are available, but employers are increasingly prioritising experienced professionals over fresh graduates. The shift toward outcome-based consulting means clients now demand measurable business results. The firm did not specify how graduates should acquire experience without a first job.

EY India faces leadership exits in consulting division
stories.summary: Manish Makhija, the leader of EY India's technology consulting business, is leaving the firm after 14 years. Mritunjay Kapoor, the leader of consulting markets, is also departing. The firm is currently managing these leadership changes as it navigates growth in its largest service line.

stories.title: Comparing MBA programs at FMS Delhi and JBIMS Mumbai
stories.summary: FMS Delhi and JBIMS Mumbai remain two of the most prominent management schools in India. Both offer strong placement opportunities and industry exposure for MBA aspirants. Choosing between the two institutions involves weighing differences in fees, entrance cutoffs, and alumni networks.

stories.title: Accenture and Google Cloud to launch AI labs in Indian schools
stories.summary: Accenture LearnVantage and Google Cloud plan to establish AI laboratories and Centres of Excellence across 1,000 Indian schools and colleges. The programme will offer training in generative and agentic AI. The companies have not yet disclosed which institutions will participate in the rollout.
